title: Idempotency
summary: Idempotency lets repeated attempts at one logical operation avoid duplicating its intended effect.
overview: A service can associate a caller-supplied request key with an operation and its result. The deduplication record and mutation need coordinated persistence to avoid gaps during failure.
why: A client may retry after the server committed a change but its response was lost.
example: An order service returns the existing order when the same checkout key is retried, and rejects that key if the cart parameters differ.
judgment: Define logical request identity, key retention, and behavior for concurrent duplicates.
next: What happens when two identical keys arrive before either request has committed?
